title: Compact Model & Route Performance Canvas — behavioral spec and chart atlas
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: Create a compact, scannable performance canvas for per-model and per-route views in Redwood Console. The canvas focuses on latency distributions, throughput trends, token-level cost/volume, and outlier microtraces. Target users are SREs, ML Engineers, and Product owners who need a quick health check and a curated drill-path into traces and rollouts. The deliverable is a behavioral spec + chart atlas describing component states, data sources, sampling strategies, and interaction patterns for slow/fast paths.
scope: Per-model overview (single model): latency p50/p95/p99, requests/s, avg tokens/request, token-cost estimate
Per-route overview (route within model): same metrics, plus route-level failure/success ratios and fallback rate
Compact visualization layer that fits in a single Console card without horizontal scroll
Microtrace peek: single-row token-waterfall preview that opens to full trace
Chart atlas with recommended aggregations, downsampling rules, and color tokens
out_of_scope: Long-term raw data retention UI changes
success_metrics: Reduction in time-to-detect latency regressions by 35% in experiment
>60% of active console users report canvas as primary first-screen for performance troubleshooting
No new backend endpoints required (use existing telemetry + sampled traces)
acceptance_criteria: Design assets (Figma) include responsive canvas for card widths 480px, 720px, 960px
Chart atlas lists aggregation window defaults (1m/5m/1h) and downsample rules per metric
Interactive token-waterfall supports hover-to-highlight tokens and click-to-open-full-trace
Accessibility: color contrast passes AA; charts include text alternatives and keyboard focus states
Hand-off doc contains component tokens, interactions, and JSON payload examples for eng
design_notes: Use 3-tier latency visualization: trend sparkline + distribution violin + recent summary numbers
Violin preferred to boxplot for showing tail mass (p99) in compact height
Token-cost layer uses stacked area for user tokens vs system tokens with cost-per-token annotation
When requests/sec is high, default to density-sampled microtraces (1% reservoir) with priority to p99 events
Rollout-aware mode: overlay canary vs stable lines when route is in a rollout; show percentage traffic split
Compact card flip interaction: summary front, detailed interactive charts on the back (preserves dashboard real-estate)
On hover of distribution chart, show estimated cost impact if p95 shifts by +10ms
Colors: latency palette anchored on '--redwood-latency-low' to '--redwood-latency-high'; maintain color-blind friendly variants
Ensure token waterfall aligns tokens to request positions; include token latency heatmap layer for batching artifacts
Prefer continuous streaming for recent 2m window; fall back to aggregated points for older windows
chart_atlas: Latency trend: line sparkline; aggregation: 1m default; rollup: avg/p50/p95/p99; tooltip: sample count & timeframe
Latency distribution: violin + median line; data: last 30m sample; render height: 64px; annotate p95 and p99
Requests/sec: stacked bar for inbound vs cached; window: 1m; legend micro-interactions to toggle cached series
Tokens/request: bar with avg & 95th percentile overlay; used to estimate token units billed
Token cost estimate: stacked area; unit price pulled from pricing config; show estimated cost per 1000 requests
Microtrace token-waterfall: fixed-height horizontal waterfall; samples: reservoir-sampled traces biased to tail; click to open trace panel
Fallback & error rate: small multiple sparkline with absolute counts + percentage; critical threshold color change at >2%
Rollout overlay: secondary line (dashed) representing canary; shading represents traffic split
data_contracts: Microtraces: traces.sample(model,route,selector) -> list of trace objects (engine will provide sampled traces only)
interactions: Default canvas shows last 30m; user can switch to 6h/24h/7d
Hover latency distribution to lock tooltip; click on percentile opens comparison drawer
Keyboard nav: tab focuses chart, arrow keys move between series, Enter expands trace
Drill-path: card -> expanded canvas -> full model timeline -> trace inspector
Annotations: allow pinned notes from SRE (manual) and automated alerts linked to time ranges
